messages:
maya: Quick check — I'm updating the Dedicated docs to migrate the old autoscale YAML to the new unified scalepolicy schema. Opening a tiny PR with example YAML + SDK snippet. Can someone sanity-check the example and SLA wording?

sam: Heads-up — the runtime now expects cooldown_seconds (seconds) not cooldown_ms. Also preemption semantics changed a bit in the last release.

eli: Can you paste the minimal YAML you want to include? I can turn it into Python + Terraform snippets.

maya: Pasting the minimal example I'm planning to add in the provisioning guide:
```yaml
scalepolicy:
  min_replicas: 2
  max_replicas: 20
  metric: rps
  target: 500
  cooldown_seconds: 120
  preemption_policy: relaxed
```

eli: OK converting to SDK example (Python). This is intentionally short for docs copy:
```python
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient()
client.set_scalepolicy(tenant_id='tenant-123', policy={
  'min_replicas': 2,
  'max_replicas': 20,
  'metric': 'rps',
  'target': 500,
  'cooldown_seconds': 120,
  'preemption_policy': 'relaxed'
})
```

sam: small nit: method name is `set_scalepolicy` (good), and the runtime will coerce `metric: rps` into the internal counter; maybe add a comment that bursty traffic can still spike token cost.

eli: adding a Terraform snippet for infra folks:
```hcl
resource "redwood_scalepolicy" "acme" {
  tenant_id       = "tenant-123"
  min_replicas    = 2
  max_replicas    = 20
  metric          = "rps"
  target          = 500
  cooldown_seconds = 120
  preemption_policy = "relaxed"
}
```

rachel: Quick question: if we document `preemption_policy: relaxed`, does that change SLA language? Need a one-sentence doc-safe line.

sam: TL;DR: SLA applies to reserved capacity commitments and availability of the Dedicated pool. `preemption_policy: relaxed` affects individual job placement during region surge (best-effort fallback to lower-priority hosts) but doesn't change the contractual uptime for a reserved pool. Suggested wording: "Preemption policy controls placement priority under capacity pressure; it may increase the chance of transient eviction for individual workloads but does not alter reserved-pool uptime SLAs."

maya: That wording is perfect, will add under "SLA & isolation" section. Also planning a short callout: "If you require strict non-preemption, set `preemption_policy: strict` and contact support for capacity guarantees."

eli: One more doc nit — mention units for cooldown explicitly (seconds). People keep using ms in older snippets.

maya: Will add a small migration note: "If migrating from older `autoscale_policy` docs: rename `cooldown_ms` -> `cooldown_seconds` and convert units (divide by 1000). Also map `autoscale_policy.preempt` -> `scalepolicy.preemption_policy` with values `strict|relaxed`."

deploy-bot: docs-preview updated for PR #2389 — staging link: https://staging-docs.redwood.ai/pr-2389 

sam: Quick QA ask — can someone run the traffic sim with the new policy to verify target -> replica mapping? I can run infra sim tomorrow AM.

eli: I can validate the snippets and push a tiny lint PR for code fencing / copy tweaks after merge.

maya: Thanks all — I'll incorporate the wording, add the two snippets, and merge once preview looks OK. :thumbsup:

sam: :thumbsup: thanks.

rachel: LGTM for SLA text, thanks for pulling this together.

maya: Merged PR and added a short example to the onboarding checklist. Closing here after prod-preview looks green.
